 Updated: 3:55 PM EDT Oct 22, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Graham Cawthon Digital Media Manager SAVANNAH, Ga. — Above video: Record Halloween spending has Savannah shoppers stretching budgets 
 Check out your local forecast here and download the WJCL App 
 Advertisement Halloween costumes may not need many extra layers this year.
 While still more than a week away, WJCL's 10-day forecast offers a glimpse of what we could expect on Oct. 31 across Southeast Georgia and the South Carolina Lowcountry.
 Savannah’s inland forecast shows a high near 79 degrees and a nighttime low around 62.
 That puts temperatures near seasonal averages.
 Trunk or Treat List: From Savannah to Port Royal, events bring first responders, pets and family fun What to expect Halloween evening
 Although an exact hourly forecast is not yet available, temperatures should begin falling through the 60s after sunset if the current outlook holds. Coastal communities, including Hilton Head Island and Tybee Island, could remain slightly milder than inland locations.
 The preliminary forecast does show a slight rain threat. While WJCL’s 10-day outlook shows a slight risk for scattered showers on Halloween, don't let that discourage neighborhood celebrations, outdoor festivals and families planning to go door to door.
 A light jacket could still come in handy later in the evening, particularly in inland communities where temperatures tend to fall faster after dark.
 A quiet stretch leading into the holiday
 We should see a generally dry and sunny pattern through the final week of October. Highs are expected to climb gradually from the mid-70s into the upper 70s and around 80 before settling near 79 on Halloween.
 The upcoming weekend will be cooler and breezy, with northeast wind gusts potentially reaching 20 to 30 mph and the strongest winds near the coast. Those winds could also contribute to minor or moderate coastal flooding around high tide.
 Conditions are expected to become calmer next week, however, with plenty of sunshine and afternoon temperatures in the mid- to upper 70s.
 The forecast could still change
 Halloween remains more than a week away, so details involving clouds, wind and the timing of any weather systems could shift. Forecast confidence generally improves within about five to seven days.
 The WJCL 22 Weather team includes Chief Meteorologist Jeremy Nelson , Jonathan Myers , Catherine Liberta , Melissa Hall and Austin Green .
